summary: District 9 is largely suburban southwest San José, including Willow Glen, Hillsdale, and Cambrian Park. The seat is open: Vice Mayor Pam Foley is termed out in December. No one won a majority in the June 2 primary, so the top two meet in a November runoff: Genny Altwer, a marriage and family therapist and former San Mateo police officer (35.5%), and Gordon Chester, a longtime San José Public Works employee (22.2%). Foley's chief of staff Scott Hughes (18.9%) and entrepreneur Mike Hennessy (17.8%) were eliminated.

positions.stance: Campaigns on crime, the cost of housing, and homelessness; frames the race as "real plans and results" versus "more of the same". (San José Spotlight)
Business-aligned; endorsed by Mayor Matt Mahan, Rep. Sam Liccardo, Vice Mayor Pam Foley, several San José business groups, the police officers' union, and Planned Parenthood. (San José Spotlight)
Affordability through more home building; lower the cost of affordable housing; incentives for senior housing. Endorsed by YIMBY Action. (San José Spotlight; YIMBY Action)
Shift homelessness money toward permanent supportive housing rather than mainly temporary shelter, and expand work opportunities for people in shelters. (San José Spotlight)
Safer crosswalks, wider sidewalks, better transit shelters, and walkable neighborhoods. (San José Spotlight)
Labor-aligned; endorsed by state Sen. Dave Cortese, Councilmember David Cohen, the Santa Clara County Democratic Party, and the South Bay Progressive Alliance. (San José Spotlight)

key_differences: This is San José's usual split between the mayor's business-aligned bloc (Altwer) and the labor-aligned bloc (Chester). The winner affects which side controls the council majority.
Altwer leads on public safety, drawing on 13 years as a police officer; Chester leads on housing supply and street design, drawing on his decade in the city's Public Works department.

Money: Altwer had raised $183,216 (including a $15,000 personal loan) to Chester's $54,775 (including a $4,000 loan). Chester's campaign says 66% of its post-July contributions were $100 or less, and has pointed out that five Altwer donors hold leadership roles on the county Republican central committee. (San José Spotlight)
In July, Altwer's campaign removed an endorsement from eliminated rival Mike Hennessy after he said he had never given it. Hennessy called it a misunderstanding. (San José Spotlight)
